title: Communication-aware dynamic graph learning for V2X misbehavior detection using GAT–BiLSTM and bagged trees
content:
by Yuee Zhang, Ping Wang, Xinyu Wang, Xiao Zheng

Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication supports cooperative driving, which also makes the malicious vehicle-state reports influence nearby vehicles. Due to the isolated use of physical state and cross-time communication context, existing methods struggle to detect malicious reports that are physically self-consistent and only reveal inconsistencies at the temporal communication level. Thus, this paper proposes a sequence-level misbehavior detection framework based on graph attention networks (GAT) and bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM). Recorded sender–receiver interactions define a directed communication graph for each one-second window. The GAT can learn the neighboring information contributes to detection. The BiLSTM captures changes across ten consecutive graph snapshots. The resulting representation is fused with physical statistics. Then, a bagged-tree ensemble is introduced to classify it. Experiments on curated VeReMi NextGen data distinguish normal behavior from three attack types. These are position offset, speed offset and data replay. Across ten random seeds the method achieves 96.40 ± 0.49% accuracy and 96.42 ± 0.48% Macro-F1. Compared with Physical features + Trees, the paired mean improvements are approximately 0.61 percentage points in accuracy and 0.62 percentage points in Macro-F1. The corresponding 95% confidence intervals exclude zero. Ablation results identify physical statistics as the main source of detection information. Combined with these statistics, the learned representation can provide a modest additional gain. Further tests show higher detection scores under feature-space Gaussian noise and changes in attack-related feature magnitude. Additional tests examine sensitivity to cross-class window substitution. Non-overlapping evaluation produces only a small decline in detection performance.
